title: Impedance-match authorizer and audit lifecycle
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement a unified policy evaluation engine and lightweight authorization middleware that performs an "impedance-match" between API/runtime/console call surfaces and the RBAC v2 rule model. Deliverables: a) efficient evaluator library (Go) with pluggable cache + metrics hooks; b) middleware adapters for API gateway, runtime request path, and console backend; c) end-to-end audit event lifecycle (ingest, redact, enrich, forward to audit-sink); d) admin controls for rule preview, dry-run, and gradual rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Evaluator library exposes deterministic Evaluate(subject, resource, action, context) API with <=2ms median latency on 99th-percentile of production-like rule sets
Middleware adapters enforce allow/deny decisions and produce audit events for every decision (permit/deny/indeterminate) with configurable redact rules
Policy cache reduces repeated full-eval calls by at least 40% on replayed requests without violating freshness window
Canary rollout flow: admin can opt-in rule set in dry-run mode and surface summary diffs in Console before flipping enforcement
Integration tests covering API gateway, runtime, and console flows with synthetic multi-tenant scenarios
Audit events land in audit-sink and include standardized fields (actor, resource, action, decision, proto_version, rule_version, request_id, truncated_payload)
Security review sign-off and threat modelling completed and documented in Confluence
tasks: Design evaluator API and wireframe cache invalidation semantics (owner: Liam)
Prototype evaluator core using existing policy-ast library and benchmark on 1000-rule corpus (owner: Priya)
Implement middleware adapter for API gateway (gRPC/HTTP) that decorates request context with decision and audit metadata (owner: Marco)
Runtime adapter: integrate evaluator into serving runtime fast-path with non-blocking KV cache (owner: Yuna)
Console backend adapter: add rule-preview endpoint, dry-run toggle, and diff snapshot export (owner: Nadia)
Audit pipeline: enrich events, apply redact rules, add envelope and forward to audit-sink (owner: DevOps Team)
End-to-end tests and performance targets validation (owner: QA)
Prepare migration guide and admin UX copy for Console (owner: PM)
Security/threat modelling session and remediation backlog (owner: Security)
Create rollout plan (canary groups, metrics, abort conditions) and coordinate with infra for capacity (owner: SRE)
decisions: Use Go for evaluator core to share runtime language with serving runtime and minimize cross-language bindings
Support both synchronous Evaluate() calls and async prefetch suggestions for warm-up; prefer synchronous for enforcement paths
Audit events will be JSON lines with an envelope schema v1; redact sensitive fields early in the middleware to avoid leaking PII
Cache freshness window default = 30s with config override per-tenant; chosen for balance between staleness and cost
Rule language remains declarative JSON+expressions; we will not introduce a separate DSL in this iteration to reduce cognitive overhead for admin teams
comments: 2026-02-20 Aisha Khan: Created ticket. Goal is to unify prior ad-hoc authorizers and ensure consistent audit semantics across products. Linking related exploration notes: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRV/RBAC+v2+Exploration

2026-02-25 Liam Ortega: Spike complete. Prototype evaluator returns decisions in ~0.8ms median and 3.1ms P99 on local 8-core bench with 800 rules. Cache layer (LRU) reduces evals by ~52% on replayed traces. Pushed prototype to GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/authorizer-proto/pull/42
2026-03-01 Security review (initial): Requested threat model for admin dry-run endpoints (possible data exposure in diffs). Action: add redact rules and require admin role for diff access.

2026-03-04 Marco: Middleware adapter sketch posted. It returns 401/403/500 mapping with clear decision reason and includes request_id header 'x-rw-request-id' in audit payload. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/775

2026-03-08 Yuna: Integrated evaluator into runtime fast-path. Observed 7% tail latency regression under synthetic load when cache disabled. Plan: non-blocking prefetch and kernel-level batching to mitigate. Filed follow-up perf task ENG-730412.

2026-03-12 Nadia (Design): Console mockups for rule preview and dry-run UI uploaded: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-RulePreview. Need wording review for 'dry-run' vs 'preview' to avoid confusion.

2026-03-14 SRE: Canary rollout plan approved pending capacity reservation. Abort condition: >0.5% unexpected denies for top 5 routes or tail latency increase >15% over baseline. Added to rollout doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRV/RBAC+v2+Rollout
notes: Keep administrator-facing APIs idempotent and rate-limited to avoid accidental rule churn
Plan for a migration window where both v1 and v2 authorizers can run side-by-side; route by tenant flag
Include per-decision explainability metadata for debugging (rule_id, evaluation_path) but redact in audit for PII-sensitive flows
